text: Question: A 55-year-old client arrived to the outpatient clinic for an annual visit and the nurse is planning to teach about enhancing the quality of life. Which of the following actions should the nurse implement first?
A. Adapt teaching modalities to the client’s sensory limitations.
B. Encourage the client to set goals.
C. Promote the client to learn independently about work-life-balance.
D. Shorten the client’s teaching sessions.
Correct answer: B. Encourage the client to set goals.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Encourage the client to set goals.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Encourage the client to set goals.” – Collaborative goal-setting guides teaching
Not correct:
• “Adapt teaching modalities to the client’s sensory limitations.” – No sensory limitation stated
• “Promote the client to learn independently about work-life-balance.” – Independent learning follows goal-setting
• “Shorten the client’s teaching sessions.” – No need to shorten sessions absent limitations

text: Question: A patient with Grave's disease exhibits tachycardia, heat intolerance, and exophthalmos. Prior to surgery, which drug is used to alter thyroid hormone levels?
A. Propylthiouracil
B. Thyroid
C. Propranolol
D. Liotrix
Correct answer: A. Propylthiouracil
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Propylthiouracil
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Propylthiouracil” – Inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis and peripheral T4 conversion
Not correct:
• “Thyroid” – Would replace thyroid hormone
• “Propranolol” – Controls adrenergic symptoms rather than synthesis
• “Liotrix” – Thyroid replacement hormone

Propylthiouracil is an antithyroid drug like the methimazole on your slide (it is not named there); your slide also says iodine is given before surgery.

text: Question: A client who takes high-dose aspirin to treat arthritis will need to take prednisone to treat an acute flare of symptoms. What action will the nurse perform?
A. Monitor closely for increased urine output.
B. Observe the patient for hypotension.
C. Observe the patient for hypoglycemia.
D. Request an order for enteric-coated aspirin.
Correct answer: D. Request an order for enteric-coated aspirin.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Request an order for enteric-coated aspirin.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)

• “Request an order for enteric-coated aspirin.” – Source expects GI protection; enteric coating does not eliminate bleeding risk
Not correct:
• “Monitor closely for increased urine output.” – Not primary interaction concern
• “Observe the patient for hypotension.” – Not primary interaction concern
• “Observe the patient for hypoglycemia.” – Prednisone more often raises glucose

text: Question: The nurse is teaching a client about home administration of insulin. The client will receive regular and NPH insulin at 0700 every day. What is important to teach this client?

B. “Draw up the medications after mixing them in a vial.”

Correct answer: C. “Draw up the regular insulin first.”
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:

B. "I may need to reduce my insulin."
C. "Diabetes is the leading cause of kidney failure."

Correct answer: A. "I need less insulin, so I am getting better."
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• "I need less insulin, so I am getting better."

slides.title: Which comment by a 12-year-old child with type 1 diabetes indicates deficient kn
text: Question: Which comment by a 12-year-old child with type 1 diabetes indicates deficient knowledge?
A. “I rotate my insulin injection sites every time I give myself an injection.”
B. “I keep Lifesavers in my school bag in case I have a low-sugar reaction.”
C. “I keep records of my glucose levels and insulin sites and amounts.”
D. “I’ll be glad when I can take a pill for my diabetes like my uncle does.”
Correct answer: D. “I’ll be glad when I can take a pill for my diabetes like my uncle does.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “I’ll be glad when I can take a pill for my diabetes like my uncle does.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““I’ll be glad when I can take a pill for my diabetes like my uncle does.”” – Type 1 diabetes requires insulin replacement
Not correct:
• ““I rotate my insulin injection sites every time I give myself an injection.”” – Rotation helps prevent lipodystrophy
• ““I keep Lifesavers in my school bag in case I have a low-sugar reaction.”” – Fast sugar helps treat hypoglycemia
• ““I keep records of my glucose levels and insulin sites and amounts.”” – Logs support dosing and monitoring
